target_customer: Consumers who need a will without hiring a lawyer; later MetLife group legal plan customers
problem: Most adults have no will because lawyers are costly and the process is unpleasant.
business_model: Free will creation, with planned revenue from a funeral home comparison platform; later documents and plans sold to consumers and employers
product_category: Online estate planning and legal documents

founders.name: Eliam Medina
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2015 says he was motivated by a hard experience arranging a family member's final arrangements.

founders.name: Rob Dyson
founders.background_notes: No further background in the opened sources.

exit.reason: Terms undisclosed. MetLife said the deal added digital capabilities complementing its Hyatt Legal plans.

competitors.name: LegalZoom
competitors.what: Online legal document service including wills

technical_complexity.rationale: Question-driven document generation with state-specific legal templates is standard engineering; the hard part is legal accuracy across states.

defensibility.rationale: Templates and flows are easy to copy and incumbents like LegalZoom already sold similar documents; a free price point was the wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept their position, and the startup sold to MetLife in November 2019.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in July 2015 framed wills as something most people lack and positioned Willing as a free alternative to paid services.

branding.domain_note: Used willing.com; acquisition of the domain was not found.

identity.logo: Not described in the sources found
identity.voice_and_tone: Approachable, plain language about a difficult subject

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly real word fits wills and the readiness it asks of users, but the sources show no community, mascot or press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Willing launched free online wills in 2015 with YC, 500 Startups and Sound Ventures, and later said it helped over half a million families according to a search summary of MetLife coverage. MetLife bought it in November 2019 with undisclosed terms to add digital estate planning to its legal plans. The consumer site was later shut down according to the live page, so the outcome looks like a technology and team acquisition by an insurer rather than a venture-scale exit.
notes: The MetLife press release URL returned 404 when fetched, so the exit is cited to the MetLife 2020 10-K, seen as a search result with a snippet naming the November 2019 completion of the Bequest, Inc. (d/b/a Willing) acquisition. A search summary of coverage said Willing had about seven people and had raised roughly $7M across two rounds; CB Insights lists about $120K. These conflict and are unverified, so only the 2015 seed with no amount is recorded. The live willing.com page says Willing has permanently shut down. Competitors come from the 2015 TechCrunch launch piece. No source states why the consumer product was folded after the acquisition, so failure factors are empty.
